france24fr.description: Un match de la France à rallonge, une qualification bleue pour les 16es de finale, Messi recordman du nombre de buts en Coupe du monde… Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Norvège en 16es de finale, le Sénégal au bord de l'élimination
france24fr.description: Le Sénégal s'est incliné dans le choc face à la Norvège (2-3) lundi au MetLife Stadium dans le New Jersey, quelques jours après une première défaite concédée face à la France (1-3) dans la même enceinte. Avec toujours aucun point au compteur, les Lions de la Teranga devront réagir lors de la troisième journée pour espérer se qualifier, alors que la Norvège est assurée de disputer les 16es de finale et jouera la première place du groupe face à la France.

france24fr.title: Jordanie - Algérie : les Fennecs dominent l'Al-Nashama et peuvent encore croire aux 16e de finale
france24fr.description: D'abord battue par l'Argentine, l'Algérie a retrouvé des couleurs face à la Jordanie, mardi. Les Fennecs ont inscrit deux buts sur corner en deuxième mi-temps après avoir été menés au score. Revivez ce match de Coupe du monde grâce à notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: En Bolivie, les barrages routiers progressivement levés après sept semaines de crise
france24fr.description: Les derniers barrages routiers étaient progressivement en train d'être levés lundi en Bolivie après l'annonce d'une trêve temporaire par l'ancien président Evo Morales, trois jours après la proclamation de l'état d'exception visant à mettre fin à plus de sept semaines de contestation.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : plus de 1000 cas confirmés
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, l’épidémie d’Ebola poursuit sa progression. Les autorités sanitaires recensent désormais 1 003 cas confirmés et 254 décès au dernier bilan, franchissant pour la première fois le seuil des mille contaminations.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la France foudroie l'Irak et se qualifie pour les 16es de finale
Mondial 2026 : la France foudroie l'Irak et se qualifie pour les 16es de finale
france24fr.description: Malgré un match perturbé par un orage et interrompu pendant plus de deux heures à la mi-temps, l'équipe de France a balayé lundi sans difficulté l'Irak (3-0) à Philadelphie pour son deuxième match disputé lors de ce Mondial. Le capitaine français Kylian Mbappé s'est offert un doublé (14e, 54e) pour devenir le second meilleur buteur de l'histoire de la Coupe du monde à égalité avec l'Allemand Miroslav Klose (16 buts).

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : à Dakar, la pression monte à quelques minutes de Sénégal-Norvège
france24fr.description: La pression monte à Dakar, à quelques minutes du coup d'envoi de la rencontre entre le Sénégal et la Norvège. Au pied du Monument de la Renaissance, les supporters des Lions de la Teranga donnent de la voix. Entre ferveur et confiance, l'ambiance est à son comble dans la fan zone.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Sénégal veut se relancer face à la Norvège
france24fr.description: Le Sénégal joue gros face à la Norvège après son revers contre la France. Cette rencontre cruciale intervient sur fond de turbulences extra-sportives révélées par Sport News Africa. Malgré ce contexte, l'espoir reste intact chez les supporters des Lions de la Teranga à Dakar.

france24fr.title: Norvège - Sénégal : revivez la qualification d'Erling Haaland et ses coéquipiers en 16es de finale
france24fr.description: La Norvège est sortie victorieuse du choc face au Sénégal (3-2) au MetLife Stadium à l'occasion de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes de la Coupe du monde 2026. Les Norvégiens sont qualifiés pour les 16es de finale, alors que la tâche se complique pour le Sénégal qui n'a plus le droit à l'erreur et devra gagner lors de la troisième journée. Revivez la rencontre avec notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: Instabilité historique au Royaume-Uni : 7 Premiers ministres en 10 ans !
france24fr.description: Avec le départ annoncé du travailliste Keir Starmer, l'instabilité politique se poursuit au Royaume-Uni qui s'apprête à connaître son septième Premier ministre en 10 ans. Un record ! Il a commis des erreurs notables, comme celle de nommer Peter Mandelson ambassadeur à Washington. Il avait été limogé neuf mois plus tard après des révélations sur son amitié avec le criminel sexuel Jeffrey Epstein.

france24fr.title: La Roumanie cherche toujours un nouveau Premier ministre après l'échec d'Adrian Vestea
france24fr.description: La crise politique continue en Roumanie : près de deux mois après la chute du gouvernement d'Ilie Bolojan, le libéral Adrian Vestea a échoué lundi à se faire élire par le Parlement. Le président Dan devrait maintenant proposer un autre nom pour diriger le pays.

zeit.title: Fußballweltmeisterschaft: Norwegen ist weiter, auch Frankreich und Argentinien in K.-o.-Runde
zeit.description: Messi, Haaland und Mbappé prägen die Siege ihrer Teams. Ein Gewitter sorgt beim Frankreichspiel für eine lange Unterbrechung. Jordanien scheidet aus. Das war die WM-Nacht

zeit.title: Treibstoffmangel: Mexiko will wieder Öl nach Kuba liefern
zeit.description: Kuba leidet unter ausbleibenden Öllieferungen aus Venezuela und Mexiko. Präsidentin Claudia Sheinbaum will nun über private Firmen Öl an den Karibikstaat liefern lassen.

zeit.title: Rente: Rentenkommission will 48-Prozent-Garantie für laufende Renten beenden
zeit.description: Die Rentenkommission empfiehlt ein Ende der Haltelinie, zeigt der Bericht, der der ZEIT vorliegt. Dies könnte das Rentenniveau für Babyboomer senken.

zeit.title: Elektroautos: Jeder fünfte EU-Neuwagen fährt rein elektrisch
zeit.description: Der Absatz von Elektroautos ist in der EU deutlich gestiegen. Auch Hybride legten zu. Besonders chinesische Anbieter konnten ihre Verkäufe steigern.

zeit.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Algerien jubelt – und hat jetzt sein Endspiel gegen Österreich
zeit.description: Für Jordanien bedeutet die Niederlage gegen Algerien das WM-Aus. Frankreichs Stürmer Kylian Mbappé erzielt sein 16. WM-Tor im Spiel gegen den Irak. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Wetter: Hitzewelle hält an: Hessen steuert auf 40 Grad zu
Fußball-WM: Das war die WM-Nacht: Frankreich gewinnt Regenschlacht
Wetter: Temperaturen steigen am Freitag auf bis zu 40 Grad
Wetter: Hohe Waldbrandgefahr in weiten Teilen Sachsen-Anhalts
Badeunfälle: Drei Tote aus dem Rhein in Hessen geborgen
Organspende: Patientenbeauftragter fordert Widerspruchslösung bei Organspende
zeit.description: In Deutschland werden zu wenige Organe gespendet. Der Patientenbeauftragte plädiert daher erneut für die Widerspruchsregel, die alle automatisch zu Spendern macht.

zeit.title: Verkehr: Nach tödlichem Lastwagen-Unfall: A6 bei Nürnberg gesperrt
Feuer in Thorstorf: 85-Jähriger aus brennendem Haus in Sicherheit gebracht
Elbvertiefung: Der tägliche Newsletter aus Hamburg: Krachen lassen? Dieser Junggesellenabschied in Hamburg hatte Folgen.
zeit.description: Die Elbvertiefung am Dienstag – Mit Zahlen zur Tanztriennale, einem Kultursenator mit zwei Gehirnen, Ärger bei einer Privatbank und dem neuen Kurs auf Kampnagel.

observador.title: Foi por um triz! Argélia acaba com o sonho da Jordânia
observador.description: Uma vitória sofrida para a Argélia e um jogo inesperado da Jordânia (1-2). O sonho jordano esteve vivo durante maior parte do jogo, através de um golo feito ao acaso, sonho esse que morreu na praia.

observador.title: Diogo Belizário: “Almodôvar pediu a uma actriz para chora...
observador.description: “Como na profissão de actor é tudo mentira, quero que a minha vida seja totalmente real”, diz Diogo Belizário que se cruzou com Rodrigo Santoro e Adrien Brody e já trabalhou com Pedro Almodôvar

observador.title: As notícias das 6h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Haaland carimba passaporte da Noruega para próxima fase
observador.description: Numa vitória suada frente ao Senegal (3-2), Erling Haaland, foi o grande destaque da partida, com dois golos junta-se a Mbappe na corrida para a bota de ouro deste mundial, liderada por Messi.

observador.title: Little Big Horn e a morte do general Custer
observador.description: É um dos momentos míticos da história do Oeste: a batalha de Little Big Horn, a 25 de Junho de 1876, onde morreu Custer e mais de 200 homens sob o seu comando, num embate brutal com vários tribos

observador.title: Messi com Mbappe no retrovisor. Francês em busca de recorde
observador.description: Na vitória francesa sobre o Iraque (3-0), Mbappe adiciona mais dois para a conta e fica apenas a dois golos de distância do recorde de Messi. Um jogo com 4 horas que carimbou a passagem francesa.

observador.title: Psílio: faz bem a quê?
observador.description: O psílio é uma fibra natural que faz gel e pode ajudar o intestino. Mas precisa de água, dose certa e cautela. A Nutricionista Mariana Chaves esclarece como usar.

observador.title: Alergia ao sol: pode aparecer de um dia para o outro?
observador.description: Sempre adorou praia e nunca teve problemas. Até ao dia em que o sol começou a deixar marcas. Afinal, é possível desenvolver alergia ao sol em adulto?

observador.title: Porque é que ninguém consegue durar em Downing Street?
observador.description: Seis primeiros-ministros em dez anos. Com Bruno Cardoso Reis, analisamos a queda de Keir Starmer, quem lhe sucede e o que explica a instabilidade política britânica.

observador.title: 4h. Irão diz que as conversações na Suiça já chegaram ao fim
observador.description: Avança que próxima fase das negociações vai envolver o Comité de Alto Nível que supervisiona a mediação. Ainda, João Cancelo diz que chegou o momento dos jogadores mostrarem a qualidade que têm.

observador.title: "Da mesma forma que errei com 20 anos, Pepe errou com 41"
observador.description: António Silva, de fora do Mundial, garante que se encontra "muito calejado" face a críticas que antes o afetavam e traça um objetivo claro para a próxima época do Benfica – estando ou não no plantel.

observador.title: Hu! Hu! Hu! Haaland trouxe o Natal mais cedo a Nova Iorque
observador.description: Noruegueses invadiram Times Square entre remadas viking e ioga, noruegueses invadiram MetLife Stadium em Nova Iorque para novo triunfo com bis de Haaland. E a invasão promete não ficar por aqui (3-2).

observador.title: 3h. Cancelo diz que jogadores vão mostrar qualidade que têm
observador.description: João Cancelo disse também em conferência de imprensa que considera injustas algumas criticas que foram feitas à equipa. Ainda, PCP diz que Governo não aprendeu a lição com o chumbo da reforma laboral.

observador.title: 2h. Martinez diz que equipa está preparada para vencer
observador.description: O Selecionador referiu também que barulho em torno da equipa portuguesa é comum, mas considera que nem tudo foi justo. Ainda, Ventura diz que PM desautorizou a ministra do Trabalho.

observador.title: Sim, Messi fica na história. Mas sim, Mbappé vai lá chegar
observador.description: França-Iraque foi o primeiro jogo do Mundial suspenso pelas condições climatéricas. Em vez de duas, demorou quatro horas. Quatro horas que se podem resumir em dois números: 16 jogos, 16 golos (3-0).

observador.title: "É o melhor de todos os tempos. Fico feliz por Messi"
observador.description: "Sobre-humano", "campeão", "génio": muitas foram as formas de descrever Messi e mais um feito histórico. Mesmo com estes elogios e mais alguns, há quem ache que pode não ser suficiente.

observador.title: O Fundo Soberano de Montenegro
observador.description: O melhor que se pode esperar do anunciado Fundo Soberano é que não aconteça, que não passe de mais um anúncio. Parece que nada aprendemos com o passado.

observador.title: Talvez seja isto o que merecemos
observador.description: A esquerda é uma força de bloqueio, nenhuma das mudanças de que o país precisa será feita com ela; o Chega juntou-se-lhe; o PSD está viciado numa forma imprestável de fazer política.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Zwei Kinder in Frankreich tot in Auto entdeckt +++ Hitzewelle in der Schweiz und Deutschland dauert an
nzz.description: Wo ist es gerade besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf Mensch und Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren, und Bränden in Europa.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Haaland trifft wieder doppelt, Norwegen vorzeitig weiter +++ Nach Unwetter-Chaos siegt Frankreich gegen Irak mit 3:0
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: Inspektoren, ein Krisenstab und eingefrorene Guthaben: Auf dem Bürgenstock gab es wenigstens ein bisschen Fortschritt
nzz.description: Nach dem Treffen in der Innerschweiz zeigen sich alle Beteiligten erfreut. Trotzdem gelang bei den Verhandlungen zwischen Iran und Amerika aber kein grosser Durchbruch. Vor allem in Libanon bleibt die Lage angespannt.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Premierminister kommen und gehen, nur der Kater Larry bleibt
nzz.description: Niemand an der Downing Street 10 in London ist länger im Amt als er: Bilder aus dem Leben von Larry, dem wohl bekanntesten Kater von Grossbritannien.

nzz.title: «Wir wollen unser Geld zurück»: Die Kantone verlangen von den Bürgern jährlich 2,65 Milliarden Franken zu viel an Steuern
nzz.description: In mehreren Kantonen fordert die Politik, den Einwohnern Überschüsse in Form von Rabatten zurückzugeben. Ein erster Kanton will die Idee nun in die Tat umsetzen.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ AKZENT» - Wie Libanon zum Zankapfel zwischen den USA und Israel geworden ist
nzz.description: Israel will sich weder von den USA noch von Iran die Bedingungen für einen Frieden in Libanon diktieren lassen. Doch genau das spaltet das wichtige Bündnis mit den Amerikanern.

nzz.title: Grossbritannien bekommt den siebten Premierminister in zehn Jahren – das Land hat nie richtig aus der Finanzkrise herausgefunden
nzz.description: Die Briten wünschen sich einen Sozialstaat wie in Deutschland, der durch Steuern und Abgaben wie in den USA finanziert werden soll. Das geht nicht auf.

nzz.title: Die Ehefrau von Spaniens Regierungschef Pedro Sánchez darf das Land nicht verlassen
nzz.description: Ministerpräsident Sánchez sieht sich einer beispiellosen Fülle von Gerichtsprozessen in seinem unmittelbaren Umfeld gegenüber. Seine Frau muss am Mittwoch sogar ihren Reisepass abgeben.

nzz.title: Flugzeuge aus Plüsch und Abschiebungen als Mitgröl-Schlager – die FPÖ provoziert mit ihrem «Remigrationssong»
nzz.description: Österreichs stärkste Partei sorgt für Kontroversen mit einem Lied, das Ausschaffungen feiert. Sie banalisiert damit einen rechtsextrem konnotierten Begriff, der anderen Rechtsaussenparteien zu radikal ist.

nzz.title: Der Weisse Adler und seine Irrflüge
nzz.description: Die Geschichte der Träger des Ordens des Weissen Adlers könnte wechselhafter und widersprüchlicher kaum sein. Die Gründe dafür liegen in unsicheren politischen Grosswetterlagen. Die Aberkennung des Ordens für Wolodimir Selenski reiht sich passend ins Bild.

nzz.title: Die Berner Gemeinde Nidau feiert mitten im Sommer Weihnachten
nzz.description: Am Bielersee setzt die reformierte Kirchgemeinde während der Hitzewelle auf Tannenbaum, Weihnachtslieder und Guetzli. Dahinter steckt ein frisch pensionierter Pfarrer.

nzz.title: Kritik an ETF und Indexfonds: SpaceX-Börsengang und starke Tech-Konzentration von Börsenindizes polarisieren
nzz.description: Im Welt-Aktienbarometer MSCI World oder dem US-Index S&P 500 hat eine kleine Zahl an Technologieaktien ein hohes Gewicht. Beobachter warnen vor Kursverlusten. Was Anleger tun sollten.

nzz.title: Johan Manzambi entzückt an der WM wie einst Xherdan Shaqiri – bald könnte er der teuerste Schweizer Fussballer sein
nzz.description: Mit 17 Jahren verliess Manzambi die Westschweiz in Richtung Deutschland, mit 20 weckt er das Interesse von internationalen Top-Klubs. Über einen, der den riskanten Weg geht.

nzz.title: Plötzlich fussballverrückt: Ein Schweizer hofft, dass Kanadas WM-Euphorie anhält – als Nationalspieler träumte er davon
nzz.description: Der Doppelbürger Daniel Imhof kickte sich aus der Provinz bis in die Bundesliga. Er blickt gespannt auf das Aufeinandertreffen seiner beiden Heimatländer und mahnt zur Bescheidenheit.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Bomben in den Alpen: Mit Siegfried Steger stirbt der letzte Südtirol-Attentäter
nzz.description: Am 23. Juni tritt das neue Verfassungsgesetz zur Reform der Südtirol-Autonomie in Kraft – ein Etappensieg im langen Kampf Südtirols für mehr Unabhängigkeit. Dieser war nicht immer friedlich. Erst Anfang 2026 starb mit Siegfried Steger das letzte Mitglied der Südtiroler «Puschtra Buibm» – für die einen Freiheitskämpfer, für die anderen Terroristen.

nzz.title: Der Abstimmungskämpfer
nzz.description: In den vergangenen Wochen fand Beat Jans ein bisschen zu sich selbst. Aber noch immer nicht zu seinem Amt.

spiegel.title: Paris: Wie mir Exil-Iraner halfen, bayerische Trachtenstrümpfe zu finden - Kolumne
spiegel.description: Deutsche Populärkultur hat es schwer in Frankreichs Hauptstadt. Doch was tun, wenn man dringend bayerische Trachtenstrümpfe braucht? Die Rettung findet sich dort, wo man sie am wenigsten vermutet.

spiegel.title: USA: Nancy Guthrie - Schreiben deutet offenbar auf Tod der Vermissten hin
spiegel.description: Ihr Schicksal bewegt viele Menschen in den USA: Seit Monaten ist die Mutter von Moderatorin Savannah Guthrie verschwunden. Nun berichten Medien über eine mutmaßliche Nachricht der Entführer.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump und sein 80. Geburtstag: Neue Details zu vereiteltem Anschlag
spiegel.description: Blutende Kämpfer, unversehrte Gäste: Das war die Bilanz der Käfigkämpfe vor dem Weißen Haus. Laut dem FBI gab es aber einen Anschlagsplan, der vereitelt wurde. Jetzt gab es weitere Festnahmen in dem Fall.

spiegel.title: E-Mobilität: Jeder fünfte Neuwagen in der EU fährt vollelektrisch
spiegel.description: Auf dem europäischen Automarkt spielen E-Autos eine immer größere Rolle. Ein Herstellerland profitiert davon besonders stark.

spiegel.title: »Compact«-Magazin: Bundestag leitet Bußgeldverfahren wegen AfD-Werbung ein
spiegel.description: Bis zu 100.000 Euro: Die Bundestagsverwaltung führt ein Verfahren gegen das als rechtsextremistisch eingestufte »Compact«-Magazin. Grund ist mutmaßliche Werbung für die AfD – obwohl die Partei die nicht wollte.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Diesen Deal kann Donald Trump sogar den eigenen Leuten nicht als Erfolg verkaufen
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident redet die Verhandlungen mit Iran schön – präsentiert für den Notfall aber schon mal einen Sündenbock. Denn ein echter Frieden liegt in weiter Ferne. Selbst in republikanischen Reihen rumort es.

spiegel.title: Smoothies: Zerstört das Mixen die Ballaststoffe in Smoothies?
spiegel.description: Püriertes Obst und Gemüse gilt als schnelle, gesunde Mahlzeit. Doch immer wieder hört man: Das Zerkleinern zerstört wertvolle Pflanzenfasern. Worauf es bei der Zubereitung ankommt.

spiegel.title: Lehrkräfte-Umfrage: Die große Angst vor politischen Debatten im Klassenzimmer
spiegel.description: Erstaunlich viele Lehrkräfte glauben nach wie vor, dass sie im Klassenzimmer politisch absolut neutral sein müssen, zeigt das neue Schulbarometer. Dabei sind sie verpflichtet, für die Demokratie einzustehen.

spiegel.title: News: Nina Warken, Gesundheitsreform, Angriff auf Schule in Minab, 10 Jahre Brexit-Referendum
spiegel.description: Wer einen Psychotherapeuten braucht, wird bald lange suchen müssen. Wie schrecklich ein Präzisionsschlag im iranischen Minab danebenging. Und was der Brexit die Briten kostet. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Erling Haaland schießt Norwegen fast im Alleingang vorzeitig in die K.-o.-Runde
spiegel.description: Dank des nächsten Doppelpacks seines Wunderstürmers ist Norwegen vorzeitig weiter. Und: »Kam mir endlos vor« – Reaktionen zur Regenschlacht beim Spiel Frankreich gegen Irak. Alles Wichtige zur WM.

spiegel.title: Fitness: So findet Ihr Kind den richtigen Sport
spiegel.description: Muss es immer Fußball sein? Wenn Kinder die Chance zum Herumprobieren bekommen, werden sie die Sportart finden, für die sie wirklich brennen.

spiegel.title: Sport bei Hitze: Wie ihr Körper vom Training im heißen Sommer profitieren kann
spiegel.description: Von Sport in der Sommerhitze wird oft abgeraten. Dabei blickt die Wissenschaft inzwischen differenzierter auf das Schweißtreiben: Hohe Temperaturen können wie ein Leistungsbooster wirken – wenn Sie diese Regeln einhalten.

spiegel.title: Diebe verursachen Rekordschaden für Einzelhandel in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Ob organisierte Banden, ganz »normale« Kunden oder gar die eigenen Beschäftigten: Im deutschen Einzelhandel wurde 2025 mehr geklaut als je zuvor. Bei den Geschäften schwindet das Vertrauen in Polizei und Gerichte.

spiegel.title: Hitze-Welle in Deutschland: Münchner sollen wegen aktueller Wetter-Lage Wasser sparen
spiegel.description: Die Menschen in München verbrauchen in der aktuellen Hitze rund ein Fünftel mehr Trinkwasser als sonst üblich. Die Stadtwerke wenden sich deshalb mit besonderen Ratschlägen an die Bevölkerung.

spiegel.title: Tesla: US-Behörde untersucht Rolle von Fahrassistenz bei tödlichem Unfall in Texas
spiegel.description: Ein Tesla kracht in Texas in ein Haus, dabei stirbt eine ältere Frau: Nun soll ermittelt werden, ob die »Full Self-Driving«-Software im Spiel war. Firmenchef Elon Musk schließt das sicherheitshalber schon einmal aus.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Kylian Mbappé bleibt Lionel Messi trotz Regen-Pause auf den Fersen
spiegel.description: Es regnete und regnete in Philadelphia, mehr als zwei Stunden dauerte die Halbzeitpause der WM-Partie zwischen Frankreich und Irak. Matchwinner war Kylian Mbappé. Er bleibt Lionel Messi auf den Fersen.

spiegel.title: US-Gericht stoppt zentrales Tool von Trumps Wahlrechtsagenda
spiegel.description: Es ist ein Rückschlag für Donald Trump vor den Zwischenwahlen: Eine Richterin untersagt die Nutzung einer von der US-Regierung aufgebauten Datenbank zur Überprüfung von Wählerlisten. Das System sei fehleranfällig.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 Live: Drei Erkenntnisse aus der längsten Halbzeit der WM
spiegel.description: Diese Hydration Break war zu lang. Michael Olise macht Frankreichs Spiel nicht nur erfolgreich, sondern schön. Und der Irak darf trotzdem zufrieden sein. Alles Wichtige im Livekommentar.

letemps.title: De la nasse comme art de gouverner
letemps.description: OPINION. Une bonne manifestation est une manifestation qui ne se tient pas. C’est bien l’horizon que dessine la nasse effectuée par la police genevoise le 14 juin. Elle ne vise ainsi plus seulement à contenir les violences, mais à rendre l’exercice d’une liberté publique suffisamment coûteux pour que les citoyens y renoncent, écrit Olivier Fillieule, spécialiste des questions de maintien de l’ordre

letemps.title: Tenu en échec par des algues, Donald Trump accuse des «fanatiques d’extrême-gauche»
letemps.description:
Rénovée en contournant les lois par l'administration Trump, la «reflecting pool» est remplie d’algues nauséabondes. Le président défend un travail «parfait» et accuse sans aucune preuve des «vandales»

«Il ne venait pas de la réparer?», s’étonne une passante en fronçant le nez. «Si, répond son mari. Mais ça n’a pas marché.» A Washington, une odeur de vase flotte autour de la reflecting

letemps.title: Podcast – Des pistes pour mieux rémunérer les artistes à l'ère de l'IA générative
letemps.description:
Le professeur de droit du numérique Yaniv Benhamou propose dans ce nouvel épisode de «IA qu'à m'expliquer» des pistes pour une meilleure redistribution de la valeur au sein de l'industrie créative, fortement mise sous pression par l'essor de l'IA générative

L’essor des grands modèles de langage représente une sérieuse menace pour les industries créatives. Les éditeurs n’hé

letemps.title: L’Europe croit que son passé est son avenir

new-sci.description: The brain undergoes a full renovation during menopause. Although these changes are profound, we’re learning that the long-term impact needn’t be all bad

new-sci.title: ‘Fusogenic’ neurosurgery let paralysed pigs walk again – are we next?
new-sci.description: Researchers say a surgery that let pigs with completely severed spinal cords walk again may lead to human trials, and then perhaps even full head or brain transplants. Columnist Helen Thomson is intrigued but sceptical of whether the technique can be successful in humans

new-sci.title: A promising natural technique to remove CO2 could backfire
new-sci.description: Several start-ups have tried to grow seaweed to remove atmospheric CO2, but this could affect the levels of nutrients in the ocean and hamper other CO2-sucking processes

new-sci.title: The surprising ways your brain changes from your 20s to your 40s
new-sci.description: When does your brain reach adulthood? We're now understanding the many ways the organ continues to mature decades after society first deems you an adult

new-sci.title: People training new AI models admit they just get chatbots to do it
new-sci.description: The next generation of AI models are meant to be trained by people paid to have conversations with them, but several of these workers have admitted to New Scientist that they simply get chatbots to do it instead. This "AI inbreeding" may reduce the power and usefulness of future models, warn experts

new-sci.title: We've found a mysterious substance on Titan and Pluto
new-sci.description: Something is absorbing light on the surfaces of Pluto and Saturn’s moon Titan, and figuring out what it is could be crucial to understanding Titan’s complex chemistry

new-sci.title: Autism may have two distinct subtypes that vary by brain activity
new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: A quantum state that lasts forever may finally be within our grasp
new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.title: The one film to watch before seeing Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day
new-sci.description: With Steven Spielberg’s new extraterrestrial film Disclosure Day just out, it’s the ideal time to watch Close Encounters of the Third Kind – perhaps the perfect UFO film, says film columnist Bethan Ackerley

new-sci.title: Faecal transplant makes the brains of old mice act young again
new-sci.description: Older mice that received a faecal microbiome transplant from younger animals went on to have improved brain plasticity, which suggests their brains could overcome a neurological condition that is typically successfully treated only in childhood

new-sci.title: Most portable air conditioners suck – but there's an easy fix
new-sci.description: Efficiency ratings on portable air conditioners don’t give consumers the full picture, and one type of aircon unit is so inefficient that it should be banned, says Michael Le Page

new-sci.title: Has the answer to life's origins been hiding in our cells all along?
new-sci.description: The surprising discovery of mysterious blobs inside our cells is revolutionising our understanding of how life works, and how it got started

new-sci.title: Gas from Uranus reveals it has an icy centre
new-sci.description: Carbon monoxide in Uranus's deep atmosphere indicates that the planet contains more ice than rock, suggesting it formed more like Neptune than we thought

new-sci.title: Can prebiotics, probiotics or postbiotics help your ageing microbiome?
new-sci.description: The disruption of your gut microbiome is a major consequence, and possible cause, of ageing. Columnist Graham Lawton looks into recent trials examining whether it can be replenished through diet and prebiotics, probiotics or postbiotics

new-sci.title: Remarkable fossils rewrite the story of how animals conquered the land
new-sci.description: Palaeontologists have found new evidence that the early ancestors of amphibians, reptiles and mammals did not have a larval stage with external gills like modern frogs or salamanders

new-sci.title: Almost the whole of Japan moved eastward after 2011 earthquake
new-sci.description: An extremely unusual tectonic movement took place 15 minutes after the Tohoku earthquake in 2011, causing almost the whole of Japan to move 5 millimetres to the east

phys-org.title: Australia has already spent more than $100 million dealing with Varroa mite. Here's what we can do next
phys-org.description: The honeybee mite, Varroa destructor, finally breached Australia's biosecurity defenses four years ago, and is here to stay. Even more concerning, our standard treatments—such as specialized pesticides—are already failing.

phys-org.title: Childhood experiences of LGBTQ+ stigma can harm romantic relationships decades later
phys-org.description: Childhood rejection, discrimination and bullying can affect your well-being as an adult. If your friends, family or community pushed you away because of your sexuality or gender, these childhood experiences of prejudice can also affect your future relationships.

phys-org.title: AI tools may reshape higher education by automating marking and personalizing feedback
phys-org.description: The evolution of higher education in the digital era has attracted global attention, and Prof. S. Joe Qin, president and Wai Kee Kau Chair Professor of Data Science at Lingnan University, published a paper titled "AI for education: The digital transformation of a liberal arts institution – implementation at Lingnan University" in the journal Computers and Education: Artificial Intelligence.

phys-org.title: Estonian-Swedish grammar challenges established theories
phys-org.description: A new doctoral thesis from the University of Gothenburg shows that a unique grammatical construction found in Estonia-Swedish dialects contradicts established assumptions about what is possible in Germanic languages.

phys-org.title: First quantum biosensor can detect rapid, invisible changes in cells
phys-org.description: In the development of diseases such as muscular dystrophy, cancer, Ebola and dengue, numerous chemical reactions take place within and between cells that contribute to disease progression. These changes can occur in less than the blink of an eye—within microseconds or faster—making them difficult to analyze. Quantum sensing offers a way to monitor these changes, helping researchers determine when, where and how rapid biological processes occur.

phys-org.title: Social inequality can harm the foundations of society
phys-org.description: Can economic inequality threaten liberal societies? This question lies at the heart of the POLAR project led by Markus Gangl, a sociologist at Goethe University Frankfurt. Several publications examining different aspects of the issue shed light on how trust in democracy, belief in meritocracy and perceptions of equal opportunity are changing.

phys-org.title: Scientists design a clay that can prevent fruits and vegetables from rotting too quickly
phys-org.description: Avocados from Chile, bananas from Costa Rica, tomatoes from southern Spain, mangoes from Brazil. A large share of the fruit and vegetables we eat have traveled across the globe before they reach store shelves here at home. But many millions of tons are lost every year before they get that far.

phys-org.title: What shapes young lives most? Everyday wins, relationships and school outrank crises
phys-org.description: Which major life events matter to young people? A study by the University of Zurich (UZH) shows that adolescents and young adults primarily cite positive, everyday developmental steps as formative events, for example, school and apprenticeships, friendships, first relationships, travel, and moving out of their parents' home. UZH researchers evaluated open-ended written responses from 1,442 participants in a long-term study. Each participant was surveyed at ages 15, 17, 20 and 24.

phys-org.title: Mosquito-borne viruses avoid killing hosts by limiting protein output, study reveals
phys-org.description: The increase in mosquito-borne virus infections is a growing public health concern. Diseases traditionally confined to tropical or subtropical regions, like dengue or West Nile virus, are expanding their geographic scope. Europe is no longer an exception, and autochthonous infections have already been recorded in Spain.

phys-org.title: Leaf-based fluorescence test speeds search for plant gene-editing targets
phys-org.description: Gene editing of plant DNA has the potential to produce crops with increased performance and resilience, but it can take a long time to achieve these gains. To shorten this process, scientists often use screening tools to determine where and how edits to the plant genome can be most effective.

phys-org.title: Making sense of Mars' tiny moon Phobos
phys-org.description: Mars' innermost moon, Phobos, has long puzzled planetary scientists, who have continually debated whether it's a captured asteroid or formed from debris after a giant impactor struck the Martian surface. The key to solving the mystery mainly rests with a better understanding of Phobos' internal structure, which unfortunately remains a "known unknown."

phys-org.title: Women negotiate as effectively as men—but leave people happier
phys-org.description: Men and women achieve similar economic outcomes in negotiations, but female negotiators foster stronger interpersonal relationships, which lead in turn to greater satisfaction with the result and a greater desire to negotiate with that woman again in the future.

phys-org.title: Nanotube-based thermoelectrics open a new pathway to waste-heat energy conversion
phys-org.description: Whenever someone asks ChatGPT a question, heat is generated somewhere in the server room—a data center. When an electric vehicle battery generates heat during operation, the heat must be managed continuously. Manufacturing processes also generate large amounts of waste heat, much of which is simply released into the atmosphere. But what if we could convert this waste heat back into electricity? Recently, a research team in Korea brought this possibility one step closer to reality.

phys-org.title: Insects exhibit evidence of a daily body clock for humidity
phys-org.description: In a novel experiment at the University of Cincinnati, researchers recently isolated kissing bugs, fruit flies, mosquitoes and spider beetles in a climate- and light-controlled environment and found that they responded predictably to cycles of humidity in the same way they do to temperature and daylight. After the humidity cue was removed, the insects continued to respond to the cyclical fluctuations of humidity and dryness established in the experiment. The study is published in the journal npj

phys-org.title: Seal pups and seabird chicks are suffering in extreme weather. How can we protect them?
phys-org.description: Extreme weather is becoming the new normal, disrupting human communities across the globe.

phys-org.title: Artificial light is keeping reef fish awake, and the effects may ripple across coral reefs
phys-org.description: Artificial light spilling into coastal waters from cities, ports, roads and hotels is disrupting sleep in coral reef fish and is associated with changes in markers linked to brain health, according to a new study from Bar-Ilan University. The paper, published in Current Biology, shows that even low levels of nighttime illumination can significantly alter the behavior and physiology of reef fish. Fish exposed to artificial light slept less, showed more fragmented sleep, became more aggressive and

phys-org.title: EU risks a crisis if it fails to halt pollinator loss, researchers warn
phys-org.description: A new white paper from eight major EU-funded pollinator projects warns that the resilience of Europe's vital societal functions and food security are at stake if the EU fails to halt and reverse wild pollinator declines and support managed pollinators. Behind the report is an interdisciplinary team of 135 leading researchers with expertise ranging from ecosystem ecology, pollinator ecology, ecological economics, social science, environmental history, behavioral psychology, political science

phys-org.title: California has lost more than half of its coastal sand dunes, first-ever assessment reveals
phys-org.description: A study conducted by UC Santa Barbara researchers and collaborators has found that California has lost more than half of its coastal dune systems. The researchers' assessment—the first of its kind for the California coast—estimates that 60% of dune systems that existed from 1850 have been lost, due to a combination of urban development, land-use changes and erosion.

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20569v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We analyze identifiability in co-adaptive human-machine systems. We show that closed-loop encoder estimates do not uniquely identify user adaptation, but instead reflect properties of the joint system. We discuss implications for interpreting behavioral adaptation and propose conditions for identification.

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20600v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: What can the success of modern AI tell us about how humans learn? This paper argues that taking AI seriously as a model of human learning supports a modest but genuine associationism. arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20622v1 Announce Type: new

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20623v1 Announce Type: new

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20625v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are promising for alpha mining via combining financial priors, symbolic reasoning, executable factor generation, and feedback-driven refinement. Yet, they face a combinatorial search space, noisy non-stationary feedback, redundant discoveries, and overfitting risks from naively reusing past successes. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20627v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Planning with world models is bottlenecked by compounding prediction errors and the difficulty of defining optimizable goals. Visual targets provide precise local gradients but poor distant guidance, while language is flexible yet limited by noisy cross-modal alignment or dependence on large generative models unsuited for the high-sampling nature of model-based planning. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20628v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans increasingly make decisions with AI assistance; for example, doctors may follow AI-recommended diagnostic tests and base their diagnoses on the results. arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20636v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) are increasingly deployed in dynamic interactive environments, creating a growing need for continual skill learning during interaction. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20637v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Electoral redistricting in Ireland's Proportional Representation Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV) system faces the challenge of selecting an optimally representative set of electoral boundaries from an enormous set of possible configurations, and where ``representative'' is a delicate balance of constitutional objectives that are often in tension with one another. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20638v1 Announce Type: new

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous vehicles offer the potential for safer and more efficient mobility, yet public trust remains limited due to the lack of transparency in their decision-making. This work addresses this issue by combining deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for adaptive driving control with large language model (LLM)-based explainability modules designed to communicate agent behavior to passengers. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20642v1 Announce Type: new

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Reversing Brexit Is Labour’s Best Hope
proj-syn.description: When it comes to the relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union, political expediency and economic logic both point in the same direction. A majority of British voters now believe that Brexit was a mistake, and they are looking for a leader who will put the issue back on the national agenda.

proj-syn.title: Global Health Reform Must Bolster Innovation
proj-syn.description: As funding falls for global public health, calls for a country-led system have grown louder. Such reforms are necessary, but they must not come at the expense of new vaccines, medicines, and diagnostics, which can be delivered by strengthening mechanisms—such as product development partnerships—that already work.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.
